events.title: The third mark beside a birth
events.body: On the same page Cailean finds the birth of Aisling entered with a mark he has seen only three or four times in a year of copying, never explained in any book given him, and recognises it for the mark the camps' whisper had already fixed to one child in the settlement.

events.title: Cailean walks to Tobar dhìreach
events.body: Rather than report to the cellar, Cailean walks the hill road to Tobar dhìreach with the seven names copied onto a scrap of paper inside his coat, to ask whether a line so old could truly be Donnchadh's own.

events.title: Cailean reads the Àth ìseal marriage line
events.body: Copying the roll of the camp at Àth ìseal in Seilear Muileann chaol, Cailean mac Eachainn reads past the first name of a marriage line for the first time in a year of copying, and finds Donnchadh mac Thormoid's line carried seven fathers back to a name far older than a hewer's line should hold.

events.title: Ealasaid of Clann na Ceiste says Sloinneadh Aisling
events.body: Ealasaid, last of Clann na Ceiste who still says the old lines at Tobar dhìreach, hears the seven names Cailean brings and gives him Aisling's whole line back to Somhairle son of Ailean Mòr, the first king, telling him plainly that she has told him whose son the child's forebear was and no more than that.

events.title: Cailean writes the line in the margin
events.body: Cailean carries Ealasaid's recital back to Muileann chaol and writes it small in the margin of the Àth ìseal roll beside Aisling's birth, telling no one at the cellar what he has done.

events.title: The custodians' first return to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir: none
events.body: When Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir orders every child with fuil-ghuail reported to An t-Àrd-mhaor's office, the custodians from Cathair dhearg to the coast make their first return and report none, though every roll among them keeps its own quiet note of such births in a physician's plain word.

events.title: A custodian of Cill ghlas answers A' Chompanaidh's agent
events.body: Asked by an agent of A' Chompanaidh whether she knows of any child with fuil-ghuail in her district, a custodian of Cill ghlas answers that she keeps no roll of miracles, only of births and deaths, and that the office is welcome to search her books for either.

events.title: Peigi Ghlas dies at Cill ghlas
events.body: Peigi Ghlas dies at Cill ghlas, her petition still unanswered, having trimmed Brìde's lamp herself the week before her death and said that she had asked Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir once and meant to leave the asking there.

events.title: Iain Maor buried at Muileann chrom
events.body: Iain Maor, third of that name to hold the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, dies in the same house he held it from and is buried within the week, the camp's custom allowing no longer delay for an office that cannot sit empty.

events.title: Mòrag hangs the staff over her hearth
events.body: Mòrag nic Iain Maor, first woman to hold the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, hangs it over her own hearth on iron hooks her father never had fitted, rather than keep it across her knees as he had.

events.title: Ruth Pallant teaches Hannah Webb the night watch
events.body: At Ceann mhòr, an old net-mender named Ruth Pallant tells the field-worker Hannah Webb of a night watch her own people's fisher-forebears learned from the island folk, kept in silence under a grey goose said to hold the sea shut. Hannah carries the telling of it home to the concession.

events.title: Hannah Webb's first vigil
events.body: In a field behind her landlord's byre near Baile chrom, Hannah Webb keeps the silent watch for the first time, and sees, or believes she sees, a pale shape cross the night sky before she sleeps through a whole night for the first time in ten years on the island.

events.title: The watch spreads along the concession's edge
events.body: Word of Hannah Webb's night vigil passes among the human labourers of the concession after a field hand sees her keeping it. Within a season a handful of others try it, and by autumn six or seven keep the field together on clear nights, spaced apart and silent.

events.title: Edward Vane dies at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir
events.body: Àrd-mhaor Edward Vane, born at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir above Ros dhomhain, dies there in the bed he was born in. The custodians who come to acknowledge the change of stewards find, as they had all his rule, that they had liked him rather more than they meant to.

events.title: The post at Tobar ghorm and the custodian's rent
events.body: A second constable post rises at Tobar ghorm. The village's custodian, Uilleam Glas, takes the rent paid for the ground and clears the village of every debt it owes A' Chompanaidh's own store, to the written complaint of A' Chompanaidh's agent.

events.title: Minister Renn writes the vigil irregular
events.body: Obadiah Renn, Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's minister at Cathair gheal's chapel, questions Hannah Webb about the watch and, finding no scripture that knows a goose, writes to Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's house that the practice is irregular and its origin uncertain, though he does not call it wrongdoing.

events.title: Baile chrom disowns the humans' watch
events.body: The custodian of Baile chrom's lower row refuses any part of the human labourers' vigil, saying the town's own name should be left out of the keeping of it. The field folk, who had hoped to call the watch a thing shared between the two peoples, learn to call it their own alone.

events.title: Manannan's priest names the goose gone astray
events.body: A priest of the harbour temple at Ceann mhòr walks to Baile chrom, watches Hannah Webb's vigil through a night, and tells her the goose she keeps is an Gèadh Fiadhaich, wandered from Manannan's own harbours into a shape no longer entirely his people's to reclaim or to stop.

events.title: The berth toll and the docker Tòmas Ruadh
events.body: A' Chompanaidh posts a new toll on every ton loaded at the Ros dhomhain coal berths. The docker Tòmas Ruadh, whom Daniel Webb once pulled clear of a falling beam, tells him of it, and the two speak for the first time of standing off the hooks together.

events.title: Merriman's constables break the stoppage
events.body: On the stoppage's tenth morning, Merriman's constables stand a rifle-line the length of the Ros dhomhain quay. The dockers, who had held nine days without a blow struck, go back to the hooks within the hour rather than test a tenth day against thirty grey coats.

events.title: The human dockers shipped over the sea
events.body: A' Chompanaidh takes the names of every human docker who struck and offers them passage over the sea within the week, once, with the plain understanding that it will not be offered twice. Hannah Webb watches her brother Daniel go up the gangway from the Ros dhomhain quay.

events.title: Raghnall Breac walks to Cill ghlas
events.body: With his knees gone stiff for the low work at Baile thais and two grandchildren to feed, the ageing hewer Raghnall Breac walks two days to the new galleries at Cill ghlas, where the pay is better and the headings still stand tall enough for a man to work upright. He writes to his daughter Eilidh twice a year.

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill given a seat at Faire nan Lòchran's table
events.body: The crew-leader Eilidh nic Raghnaill of Baile thais is asked, for the first time, to sit at the table where Faire nan Lòchran keeps its business, and copies its minutes into a second book kept in her own linen chest, where no clerk of A' Chompanaidh would think to look.

events.title: Fairley marks the custodians' asking on his plan
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's engineer Robert Fairley writes the custodians' request, that no charge be set within sight of the shrine at Cill ghlas, into the margin of his working plan. The plan shows the shrine as a bare shape with no depth drawn beneath it, and the numbered headings below are never measured against it.

events.title: Beathag Ruadh's roll at Caol ìseal
events.body: The custodian of Caol ìseal counts forty casks of blasting-powder off a ship of A' Chompanaidh, told to her carters as lamp-oil, and writes in her roll that the staves smelled of nothing when she put her hand to them. Her line goes unanswered into Seilear Muileann chaol with the rest of the year's roll.

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill at the fenced ground
events.body: Eilidh nic Raghnaill walks to Cill ghlas to find her father's grave and finds instead the fence and the fallen headgear of the eighth heading. A constable turns her away from the closed ground. She writes nothing of the hour in Faire nan Lòchran's book.

events.title: Scàineadh Cill ghlas kills the thirty-one
events.body: On the ninth of an t-Ògmhios the fault beneath Cill ghlas tears open and the ground above the eighth heading and the old shrine cutting comes down together. The custodians' roll names thirty-one dead, among them the hewer Raghnall Breac, and says four bodies more were never brought up.

events.title: A' Chompanaidh fences the closed district
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's surveyors return within the week to fence the district from Cill ghlas to Àth chaol, and Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's order forbids any wage or working on any ground inside the fence. Households leave through the autumn and winter, first in twos and threes, then whole villages together.

events.title: Fionnlagh's warning at Muileann chrom
events.body: The overseer Fionnlagh tells the new agent Edgar Holt that the flooded ground under one heading at Muileann chrom has never gone a night without its pumps, drawing as it does from an unmapped old working above it. Holt orders the pumps stopped regardless, to spare coal for the winding-gear until a delayed barge arrives.

events.title: The flooded gallery takes seven
events.body: With the pumps idle overnight, the gallery at Muileann chrom fills to the roof, and seven men of the change of shift, Fionnlagh among them, do not come up. Mòrag nic Iain Maor stands at the pit-mouth as they are brought up and laid in a row on the wet boards.

events.title: Mòrag's testimony struck from the inquiry
events.body: At Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's inquiry at Ros dhomhain, the fourth Steward Mòrag nic Iain Maor carries A' Chompanaidh's own staff into the room and testifies that Edgar Holt ordered the pumps stopped against his overseer's warning. The commissioners rule her account improper and have the clerk strike it from the record.
